name: Phinehas
title: The Zealous Priest
summary: Phinehas was the grandson of Aaron and the son of Eleazar. He is best known for his zealous act when he pierced an Israelite man and a Midianite woman during Israel's sin at Baal-Peor, which stopped a deadly plague. For his zeal, he received God's covenant of an everlasting priesthood.

keyEvents.title: Phinehas' Zealous Act at Baal-Peor
keyEvents.description: When the Israelites sinned with Moabite and Midianite women and began to worship Baal-Peor, Phinehas intervened and pierced Zimri and the Midianite woman Cozbi with a spear. This act stopped the plague that had killed 24,000 Israelites.

keyEvents.title: God's Covenant of Peace with Phinehas
keyEvents.description: God gave Phinehas a covenant of peace and promised him and his descendants an everlasting priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the children of Israel.

keyEvents.title: The War Against Midian
keyEvents.description: Phinehas was chosen by Moses to lead the holy war against the Midianites as vengeance for their attempt to lead Israel into sin. He carried the sacred utensils and the trumpets.

keyEvents.title: Phinehas as Mediator in the Dispute Over the Altar at the Jordan
keyEvents.description: When the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh built an altar by the Jordan, Phinehas was sent as leader of a delegation to investigate the matter and prevent a possible war between the tribes. His diplomatic efforts resolved the conflict peacefully.

keyEvents.title: Phinehas's Service as Priest Before the Ark of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Phinehas served as priest before God's ark of the covenant at a time when Israel sought the Lord's guidance in the war against the tribe of Benjamin.

keyEvents.title: Phinehas in the Genealogies
keyEvents.description: Phinehas is mentioned in several genealogies as an important link in the Aaronic priesthood, and his descendants served as high priests in Israel through many generations.
